usages.explain: The verb at the end of the sentence is in the past tense, to express a situation contrary to reality after assuming that a past event didn't happen in reality, or assuming a state different from reality.

examples.transcription: ひつようであればかった。
examples.mean: I bought it if I needed it.

examples.content: 時間があればもっと案内したかったです。
examples.transcription: じかんがあればもっとあんないしたかったです。
examples.mean: I wish I had more time to show you around.

examples.content: 手当てが早ければ、彼女は助かっていた。
examples.transcription: てあてがはやければ、かのじょはたすかっていた。
examples.mean: If she had been treated quickly, she could have survived.

title: …ば ... た => If ..., then would have
